intent.raw_query: Patagonia hiking Torres del Paine, $4500, 12 days, December 2026

selected_hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route that winds through the most spectacular highlights of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km, passing through Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Mirador Las Torres viewpoint. Book refugios or campsites in advance for overnight stays along the route.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to the iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine for a breathtaking sunrise. The 8-hour round-trip hike from Hotel Las Torres gains significant elevation and rewards hikers with a stunning turquoise glacial lake reflecting the three towering peaks. This is the most photographed and celebrated viewpoint in all of Patagonia.

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through icy waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of the largest glaciers in South America outside of Antarctica. A guided kayaking tour takes you up close to towering blue ice walls and floating icebergs while expert guides share insights about glacial formation and Patagonian ecosystems. A truly once-in-a-lifetime nature experience.

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Hike
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering peaks including Paine Grande and Cerro Cota 2000. The trail offers some of the most diverse and awe-inspiring scenery in the park, with frequent sightings of condors soaring overhead and the thunderous crack of calving glaciers.

experiences.name: Patagonian Wildlife Safari and Lago Sarmiento Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk along the shores of Lago Sarmiento, exploring the unique stromatolites and spotting Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, Andean condors, flamingos, and the elusive puma. A knowledgeable naturalist guide provides deep ecological context about the unique Patagonian steppe ecosystem and the park's conservation efforts.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Torres del Paine, Patagonia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled - flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled - in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Collect luggage, arrange pre-booked budget shuttle or shared transfer to Puerto Natales (approx. 1.5 hrs). Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine. Grab a light snack from any 24-hr convenience store or hotel reception if available.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or airport snack
meals.lunch: On the plane or airport food court
meals.dinner: Light snack from convenience store or vending machine near hotel upon late arrival — budget ~$5 USD

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your shuttle transfer before departure to save money and avoid taxi surcharges at night. Pack a snack in your carry-on for late-night arrival. Confirm hotel late check-in policy in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, enjoy a budget breakfast at the hotel or a nearby local café in Puerto Natales. Visit the Puerto Natales waterfront (Seno Última Esperanza) for a gentle orientation walk — free and scenic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Puerto Natales town on foot. Visit the free Museo Histórico Municipal to learn about Patagonian history and culture. Stock up on trekking supplies, snacks, and groceries at local supermarkets (Unimarc or Almacén) to save money on park meals. Rent or confirm trekking gear if needed from budget rental shops in town.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost orientation talk at a local hostel or trekking outfitter about Torres del Paine trails. Plan your trekking days and book any required park entry permits online (CLP ~21,000 per person). Enjoy a home-cooked style dinner at a local comedor or family restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — café con leche and marraqueta bread, budget ~$4 USD
meals.lunch: Self-prepared sandwich from supermarket supplies, budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: Local comedor or Restaurante El Rincón in Puerto Natales — hearty cazuela stew or lentil soup, budget ~$8-10 USD

day_by_day.notes: Buying groceries and snacks in Puerto Natales is significantly cheaper than inside the national park. Stock up on energy bars, instant noodles, dried fruit, and nuts for trail days. Download offline maps (Maps.me or Gaia GPS) for the park.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast and pack day bags. Take the budget shared bus or colectivo from Puerto Natales to Torres del Paine National Park entrance (departs ~07:30, ~2 hrs, approx. $10 USD one way). Pay park entrance fee at the gate. Begin acclimatization with a short, easy walk along Lago Sarmiento viewpoint trail — free and stunning turquoise waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mirador Cuernos trail (approx. 3-4 hrs round trip, moderate difficulty). Enjoy panoramic views of Los Cuernos peaks reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld. Bring packed lunch to eat at the lakeside viewpoint. Return to the park visitor center area.
day_by_day.evening: Return via shared bus to Puerto Natales by late afternoon. Cook a simple pasta or rice dinner using supermarket groceries at the hotel if kitchen facilities are available, or eat at a budget local eatery. Review and pack gear for the next day's longer hike.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or hostel breakfast — oats, fruit, and coffee, budget ~$4 USD
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket — sandwiches, fruit, energy bars eaten on the trail, budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta with canned tomato sauce at hotel kitchenette, or local comedor, budget ~$5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: Shared buses (Bus Sur or Buses JB) are the most budget-friendly way to enter the park. Book seats in advance during December high season. Carry at least 2 liters of water and wear layers — Patagonian weather changes rapidly.

day_by_day.morning: Very early start — depart Puerto Natales by 06:00 on the first park bus. Arrive at Laguna Amarga ranger station. Begin the iconic Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike. The trail starts at Hotel Las Torres (free public access trailhead). Hike through lenga beech forest and moraine fields — first 2 hours moderate, final ascent steep.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach the mirador at the glacial lagoon base of the Torres granite towers (approx. 4 hrs ascent). Spend 45-60 minutes at the top soaking in the dramatic scenery. Begin descent back to the trailhead (approx. 3.5 hrs). Rest at the bottom and refuel with packed snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Catch the return shared bus to Puerto Natales (departs ~18:00 from Laguna Amarga). Arrive back exhausted but exhilarated. Treat yourself to a warm, hearty dinner at a local restaurant. Rest and stretch sore muscles.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed breakfast eaten on the bus or at trailhead — oats, banana, coffee in thermos, budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch eaten at the mirador — sandwiches, nuts, chocolate, dried mango, budget ~$5 USD
meals.dinner: Restaurante La Picada or similar local spot in Puerto Natales — lamb stew or grilled chicken with rice, budget ~$10-12 USD

day_by_day.notes: This is an 8-hour round-trip hike covering approximately 18-20 km with 800m elevation gain. Start as early as possible for the best light and to avoid afternoon crowds. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots. Trekking poles are highly recommended for the rocky moraine ascent.

day_by_day.morning: Designated rest and recovery day after the strenuous Torres hike. Sleep in, enjoy a relaxed breakfast. Do gentle stretching or yoga. Visit the local Feria Artesanal market in Puerto Natales to browse handmade Patagonian crafts — free to browse, budget souvenirs available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront Costanera path (free). Watch for black-necked swans and pink flamingos on Seno Última Esperanza. Visit Cueva del Milodón Natural Monument if energy allows — a 30-min drive, shared taxis or rental available (~$15 USD round trip). See the prehistoric cave of the giant ground sloth.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales for dinner. Visit a local peña or cultural gathering if available. Repack gear and prepare for the next multi-day hike. Charge all electronics and power banks.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely café breakfast in Puerto Natales — eggs, toast, fresh juice, budget ~$6 USD
meals.lunch: Budget empanadas from a local bakery (3-4 empanadas), budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Supermarket self-catered meal or Café Indigo budget menu — vegetable soup and bread, budget ~$7 USD

day_by_day.notes: Rest days are essential in Patagonia to prevent injury during multi-day trekking. Use this time to wash clothes, restock food supplies, and update travel journal. Cueva del Milodón entry is ~$8 USD — worth it for history enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by 07:00 bus to Torres del Paine. Enter the park and head toward the Valle del Francés trailhead via the Paine Grande sector. Take the free catamaran-alternative trail along Lago Pehoé if budget is tight (the paid catamaran costs ~$40 USD — the walking route adds 2-3 hrs but is free and scenic).
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Valle del Francés Day Hike. Hike through southern beech forest into the glacially carved valley. Listen for the thunderous crack of hanging glaciers calving from the Francés Glacier. Reach Mirador Británico for stunning 360° views of the valley, glaciers, and surrounding peaks (approx. 5-6 hrs total round trip from Paine Grande).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paine Grande area. If budget camping is pre-booked, set up tent at Camping Paine Grande (approx. $10-12 USD per person). Cook a simple hot meal on a camp stove. Watch the extended Patagonian sunset over Lago Pehoé — spectacular golden light until 22:00+ in December.

meals.breakfast: Pre-packed oats with dried fruit eaten on bus, coffee in thermos, budget ~$3 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — peanut butter crackers, cheese, salami, energy bars, budget ~$5 USD
meals.dinner: Camp-cooked instant noodles with canned tuna and dried vegetables at Camping Paine Grande, budget ~$4 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Valle del Francés hike is approximately 10-12 km round trip from Paine Grande with 600m elevation gain to Mirador Británico. Pre-book camping spots at Paine Grande through CONAF or Vertice Patagonia — December fills up fast. Bring a windproof jacket as the valley creates strong gusts.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at camping Paine Grande to a stunning lakeside sunrise. Enjoy a hot camp breakfast. Pack up camp and begin trekking toward Campamento Italiano along the W Trek route. The trail follows the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld with constant views of Los Cuernos.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking east along the W route toward Campamento Los Cuernos (approx. 10 km, 3-4 hrs). Set up camp or check in to the budget refugio dorm option (~$30-35 USD per person with dinner and breakfast included — good value). Rest tired legs and explore the immediate lakeside area.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the included refugio dinner (hearty soup, main course, and dessert) if staying at Refugio Los Cuernos. Or cook camp meal if tent camping. Watch the alpenglow on Los Cuernos peaks at sunset. Socialize with fellow trekkers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Camp-cooked oatmeal with powdered milk and sugar, instant coffee, budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Packed trail snacks eaten while hiking — nuts, dried mango, crackers, budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Refugio included dinner or camp-cooked rice with lentils and spices, budget ~$3-5 USD if self-catered

day_by_day.notes: The W Trek section from Paine Grande to Los Cuernos is approximately 10 km on well-marked trails. Carry at least 3 liters of water — streams are available for refilling with a filter. The refugio dorm option, while more expensive than camping, includes meals and a warm bed which can be worth it mid-trek.

day_by_day.morning: Early start from Campamento Los Cuernos. Continue east along the W Trek toward Refugio Las Torres (approx. 11 km, 3.5-4 hrs). The trail winds through lenga beech forest and open pampa with constant views of the Paine Massif. Spot Andean condors soaring on thermals overhead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at the Las Torres sector. Drop gear at camping area (Camping Torres Central, ~$10-12 USD). Optional short afternoon hike to Cascada del Río Ascencio viewpoint (1 hr round trip, easy). Rest and prepare for the next morning's optional second Torres ascent for different lighting conditions.
day_by_day.evening: Cook dinner at the campsite communal area. Share trail stories with other W Trek hikers. Attend the free ranger-led evening talk at the Las Torres visitor center about Patagonian wildlife and conservation. Early bedtime to rest for tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Leftover camp food — crackers, peanut butter, instant coffee, budget ~$2 USD
meals.lunch: Final trail snacks from pack — energy bars, cheese, and crackers, budget ~$3 USD
meals.dinner: Camp-cooked lentil soup with bread purchased at Las Torres camp store (expensive — buy sparingly), budget ~$5-8 USD

day_by_day.notes: The Las Torres camp store sells basic supplies at a significant markup — buy all supplies in Puerto Natales. The W Trek from Paine Grande to Las Torres is approximately 31 km total over 3 days and is one of South America's most iconic multi-day hikes. Carry a first aid kit and blister treatment.

day_by_day.morning: Optional second sunrise hike to Mirador Las Torres (depart camp by 04:30 to catch first light). This time experience the towers in the golden morning light — different from the standard daytime hike. The familiar trail feels rewarding the second time. Spend 30-45 minutes at the mirador.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Las Torres camp by 10:00. Pack up all camping gear. Catch the shared bus from Laguna Amarga back to Puerto Natales (departs ~12:00-13:00). Arrive in Puerto Natales by 14:30. Check back in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Take a long hot shower — one of the best feelings after 3 days of camping.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate completing the W Trek with a sit-down dinner at a proper restaurant. Wash and dry all trekking clothes. Rest thoroughly. Browse local souvenir shops for budget-friendly gifts — locally made wool items and postcards are affordable.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn camp snack before sunrise hike — energy bar and water, budget ~$1 USD
meals.lunch: Supermarket sandwich and juice purchased upon return to Puerto Natales, budget ~$4 USD
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Restaurante Última Esperanza or similar — lamb chops or king crab (centolla) if splurging, or a budget set menu, budget ~$12-15 USD

day_by_day.notes: Completing the W Trek is a major accomplishment — celebrate appropriately! The optional second sunrise hike is highly recommended for photographers. Wash and thoroughly dry all gear before packing — damp gear in a bag leads to mold. Check for any blisters or injuries and treat them properly.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve — rest and recovery morning. Sleep in. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast. Visit the Puerto Natales weekend market or local shops for fresh produce and Christmas treats. Take a gentle walk along the waterfront to watch wildlife.
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip to Parque Nacional Bernardo O'Higgins viewpoint via a short local boat tour (budget shared tours ~$25-30 USD) or alternatively hike the free Cerro Dorotea viewpoint trail just outside Puerto Natales (2-3 hrs round trip, free, panoramic views of Seno Última Esperanza and the mountains).
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner — many local restaurants offer a special holiday menu. Join the Puerto Natales community celebrations if any are happening in the main plaza. Enjoy the festive atmosphere of a Patagonian Christmas. Call family and friends to share holiday greetings.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas Eve breakfast — fresh medialunas (croissants) and coffee at a local café, budget ~$5 USD
meals.lunch: Self-catered picnic by the waterfront with supermarket treats — cheese, crackers, fruit, chocolate, budget ~$6 USD
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve set menu at a local restaurant — typically includes soup, main, and dessert, budget ~$12-15 USD

day_by_day.notes: Cerro Dorotea is a completely free hike with spectacular views and is often overlooked by tourists — highly recommended as a gentle recovery hike. On Christmas Eve in Chile, the main celebration is the Noche Buena dinner — restaurants may be busy, book ahead. Many businesses close early on December 24.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day! Enjoy a special holiday breakfast. Take a free self-guided birdwatching walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront — spot black-necked swans, flamingos, steamer ducks, and Magellanic penguins (seasonal). Bring binoculars if available.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final visit to Torres del Paine National Park via shared bus for a lighter, scenic day hike. Hike the easy Laguna Verde and Laguna Azul loop trail (approx. 4-5 hrs, moderate) — two stunning contrasting lakes in one hike with excellent condor-spotting opportunities. Bring a packed Christmas picnic lunch.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Puerto Natales for a final Christmas dinner. Reflect on the incredible 12-day Patagonian adventure. Pack bags for departure. Review photos and journal entries from the trip. Toast to an unforgettable budget adventure in one of the world's most dramatic landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas breakfast at hotel — eggs, toast, fruit salad, hot chocolate, budget ~$7 USD
meals.lunch: Christmas picnic at Laguna Azul viewpoint — special treats from supermarket, budget ~$7 USD
meals.dinner: Final Christmas dinner at a local Puerto Natales restaurant — traditional Chilean Christmas meal or lamb asado, budget ~$13-15 USD

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Day in Chile is a national holiday — most shops and businesses are closed. Stock up on any needed supplies on December 24. The Laguna Verde/Azul area is less crowded than the main W Trek corridor and offers a peaceful final park experience. Many park buses may have reduced schedules on Christmas Day — confirm times in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia. Wake up early for a last sunrise walk along the Puerto Natales waterfront — completely free and deeply memorable. Enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a local café. Complete packing and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at hotel if checkout is before transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight departure time, take a final stroll through Puerto Natales. Visit any remaining sights or shops. Purchase last-minute souvenirs — local wool products, artisanal chocolate, and Patagonia-branded items make great gifts. Head to Punta Arenas airport via shared shuttle (book in advance, ~$12-15 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Punta Arenas airport. Reflect on an incredible 12-day budget adventure through one of Earth's most spectacular wilderness areas — the granite towers, glacial valleys, turquoise lakes, condors, and endless Patagonian sky.

meals.breakfast: Final café breakfast in Puerto Natales — coffee and fresh pastries, budget ~$5 USD
meals.lunch: Airport café or packed supermarket snacks for the journey, budget ~$5-7 USD
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your return flight details and shuttle transfer times the night before. Allow at least 3 hours before flight departure to account for the Punta Arenas transfer. Total estimated budget for the 12-day trip (excluding flights): approximately $400-550 USD including park fees, accommodation, food, transport, and activities — very achievable with careful planning and self-catering.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport on flight UA at 22:30. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine. Check in, freshen up, and settle into your Beachfront accommodation. Get a good night's rest to prepare for the adventures ahead.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Light snack or late-night bite at the resort's lounge or a pre-packed meal from the airport. Many Patagonian lodges offer a small welcome spread for late arrivals.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm transfer arrangements in advance with the resort. Pack layers for the cold Patagonian night. Keep essentials in your carry-on as luggage can be delayed. Exchange currency or withdraw Chilean pesos before leaving the airport.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. Enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning exploring the immediate resort grounds and the beachfront area — take in your first views of the Patagonian landscape, spot local birdlife such as Andean condors and flamingos, and breathe in the fresh air. Orientation walk around the property.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join the Patagonian Wildlife Safari and Lago Sarmiento Walk — a guided nature walk along the shores of Lago Sarmiento. Explore the unique and ancient stromatolites (microbial mats), observe guanacos, rheas, and other Patagonian wildlife in their natural habitat. This is a gentle, scenic introduction to the park's ecosystem. Duration approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a relaxing evening. Enjoy the extended Patagonian summer daylight (sunset around 10:00–10:30 PM in December). Sit on the beachfront terrace with a glass of Chilean wine and watch the alpenglow on the mountains.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy local cheeses, cold cuts, fresh bread, eggs, and coffee.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or light meal at the resort café before the afternoon excursion.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort restaurant — try a hearty Patagonian lamb stew (cordero al palo) or grilled trout. Mid-range pricing, approximately $25–$40 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentionally light day to acclimatize to the altitude and weather. Patagonian weather is highly unpredictable — always carry a wind shell, base layers, and sunscreen regardless of the morning forecast. Confirm booking for the W Trek starting Day 4.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at the resort (6:30–7:00 AM). Depart for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — trek to the iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine for a breathtaking sunrise experience. The trailhead begins at Hotel Las Torres. The 8-hour round-trip hike (approximately 18 km) ascends through lenga beech forest, rocky moraines, and culminates at a stunning glacial lake with the three granite towers soaring overhead.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent from Mirador Las Torres. The afternoon portion of the hike winds back through the forest — enjoy the changing light on the landscape and keep an eye out for pumas, foxes, and condors. Reach the trailhead by early-to-mid afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by shuttle or transfer. Soak tired legs and enjoy a warm shower. Spend the evening reviewing gear and repacking for the upcoming W Trek. Early dinner and an early bedtime.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — sandwiches, energy bars, dried fruit, nuts, and chocolate. Prepare the night before or request from the resort kitchen.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort — opt for a protein-rich meal such as grilled lamb chops or a hearty lentil soup with crusty bread to fuel recovery. Budget approximately $30 USD.

day_by_day.notes: Start hiking by 7:00–7:30 AM to catch the best morning light on the towers. Wear sturdy waterproof hiking boots. Bring at least 2 liters of water, trekking poles are highly recommended for the moraine section. This hike is strenuous — pace yourself on the ascent.

day_by_day.morning: Breakfast at the resort (7:00 AM). Pack your multi-day trekking bag — you will be departing for the W Trek today, a 4-5 day iconic route through Torres del Paine's most spectacular highlights. Store non-essential luggage at the resort. Transfer to the park entrance and take the catamaran or bus to the starting point of the W Trek at Lago Grey or Paine Grande depending on your chosen direction.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the W Trek — Day 1 on trail: Trek from Paine Grande camp toward the Grey Glacier. The trail (approximately 11 km one way) offers incredible views of Lago Grey, floating icebergs, and the massive Grey Glacier. Arrive at Refugio Grey or Grey Camp in the afternoon and set up your accommodation (refugio bunk or camping depending on your booking).
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Refugio Grey. Enjoy dinner at the refugio dining hall with fellow trekkers. Share trail stories and plan the next day's route. The long Patagonian evening light creates a magical atmosphere over the glacier.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail — sandwiches and snacks.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Grey dining hall — set menu typically includes soup, a main course (pasta, meat, or fish), and dessert. Budget approximately $25–$35 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: W Trek bookings (refugios and camping) must be reserved well in advance through CONAF-authorized operators. Carry cash and a credit card — some refugios accept cards but don't rely on it. Pack for all weather: rain gear, warm layers, sun protection, and gaiters. Weight your pack carefully — aim for under 10 kg.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at Refugio Grey (7:00 AM). Today's highlight: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition — paddle through the icy turquoise waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier. This guided kayaking experience (approximately 3–4 hours) takes you up close to towering ice walls and floating icebergs. Wetsuits and all equipment are provided by the guide operator.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the kayaking expedition, begin trekking back east along the Grey trail toward Paine Grande. The 11 km return trek offers different perspectives of the glacier and lago. Arrive at Paine Grande camp/refugio by mid-to-late afternoon. Check in and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Paine Grande Refugio. The evening sky over the lake and mountains is spectacular in December — enjoy the golden hour light. Rest well for the challenging Valle del Francés hike tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Set breakfast at Refugio Grey.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch consumed on the trail or at a rest point near the glacier.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Paine Grande Refugio — hearty set menu. Budget $25–$35 USD.

day_by_day.notes: The kayaking excursion must be booked in advance and is weather-dependent — have a backup plan (extended glacier viewpoint walk) in case of cancellation due to wind or rain. Patagonian winds can be extremely strong on the lake — the kayak guides will assess conditions on the day.

day_by_day.morning: Early breakfast at Paine Grande (6:30–7:00 AM). Today: Valle del Francés Day Hike — one of the most dramatic sections of the W Trek. Depart early and hike into the glacially carved Valle del Francés. The trail ascends through lenga beech forest into an amphitheater of hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and towering peaks including Paine Grande and the Cuernos del Paine. The hike to Mirador Británico (the highest viewpoint) is approximately 10–12 km one way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Mirador Británico by midday — on a clear day, the 360-degree panoramic views are absolutely breathtaking. Enjoy lunch at the viewpoint. Begin the descent back through the valley in the afternoon, listening for the thunderous crack of ice calving from the hanging glaciers above.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Paine Grande or continue trekking east to Refugio Los Cuernos (approximately 11 km from Paine Grande). Check in and enjoy a well-earned dinner. Soak in the views of the Cuernos del Paine reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld.

meals.breakfast: Set breakfast at Paine Grande Refugio.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Mirador Británico — enjoy the views while you eat.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Refugio Los Cuernos — set menu with soup and main course. Budget $25–$35 USD.

day_by_day.notes: This is the most physically demanding day of the W Trek. Start as early as possible to maximize clear weather windows — mornings in Torres del Paine are typically calmer. Watch for falling rocks in the valley. Trekking poles are essential for the steep moraine sections.

day_by_day.morning: Breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos (7:00 AM). Trek the final eastern leg of the W from Los Cuernos toward Hotel Las Torres (approximately 11 km). The trail hugs the northern shore of Lago Nordenskjöld, offering stunning views of the Cuernos and surrounding peaks. This is a moderate section — enjoy the relative ease after yesterday's challenging hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Hotel Las Torres area by early afternoon. This is the base for tomorrow's final W Trek highlight. Check into Refugio Las Torres or the campsite. Spend the afternoon resting, stretching, and preparing your gear for the pre-dawn start tomorrow. Optional: short exploratory walk around the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at the Las Torres area refugio or restaurant. Set an alarm for 4:30–5:00 AM for tomorrow's sunrise hike. Lay out all gear and pack a trail snack for the early morning ascent. Early bedtime — 9:00–9:30 PM.

meals.breakfast: Set breakfast at Refugio Los Cuernos.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the trail or light snack at Las Torres area upon arrival.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Las Torres refugio dining hall — opt for pasta or rice dishes for carbohydrate loading before tomorrow's hike. Budget $25–$35 USD.

day_by_day.notes: This is a transitional and recovery day — use it wisely. Treat any blisters and tend to sore muscles. Hydrate well. Confirm your alarm is set and that you know the trail departure point for the pre-dawn Mirador Las Torres hike. The W Trek is nearly complete!

day_by_day.morning: Wake up at 4:30 AM. Light snack and depart by 5:00 AM for the pre-dawn ascent to Mirador Las Torres — the grand finale of the W Trek. Hike by headlamp through the forest and up the rocky moraine. Arrive at the glacial lake below the towers just as the first light of dawn touches the granite spires, turning them from grey to gold to orange. A truly life-changing moment. Spend time at the mirador soaking in the view.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to Hotel Las Torres by mid-morning. Complete the W Trek — congratulations! Transfer back to Puerto Natales or directly to Aegean Bliss Resort. Arrive at the resort by early-to-mid afternoon. Shower, unpack, and do laundry. Rest and reflect on the incredible week of trekking.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner at the resort restaurant. Treat yourself to a special Patagonian meal — roasted lamb (cordero al palo), a glass of Carménère or Malbec, and a decadent dessert. You've earned it.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn trail snack (energy bar, banana, nuts) before the hike. Full breakfast at Hotel Las Torres upon return from the mirador.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Hotel Las Torres or packed snack during the transfer.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant — splurge slightly on a special Patagonian set menu. Budget $40–$55 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The W Trek is complete! This is one of the world's great multi-day hikes. The sunrise at Mirador Las Torres is the iconic finale — weather permitting, it will be unforgettable. If clouds obscure the towers, the hike is still magnificent. Celebrate your achievement this evening.

day_by_day.morning: Full rest and recovery morning. Sleep in, enjoy a slow breakfast at the resort. Spend the morning by the beachfront — read, journal, or simply stare at the mountains. Optional: gentle stretching or yoga on the terrace. Visit the resort spa if available for a massage to ease tired trekking muscles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Optional gentle excursion: Take a short drive or guided transfer to Lago Sarmiento for a relaxed afternoon walk along the shoreline. Observe the flamingos and birdlife at the lake's edge. Alternatively, explore the resort grounds and nearby viewpoints at a leisurely pace. Photography afternoon — capture the incredible Patagonian light.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset viewing from the resort beachfront — December sunsets in Patagonia occur around 10:00–10:30 PM, offering hours of golden light. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks with Chilean wine or a pisco sour on the terrace.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full buffet breakfast at the resort — take your time.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort café — try a fresh empanada, salad, or soup. Budget $10–$15 USD.
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort — try the catch of the day (fresh Patagonian trout or king crab if available). Budget $30–$40 USD.

day_by_day.notes: This is an intentional rest day after the demanding W Trek. Your body needs recovery time. Don't feel guilty about doing very little — this is part of a balanced trip. Rehydrate thoroughly and eat well to restore energy levels.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Eve — begin with a festive breakfast at the resort. Morning excursion: Guided wildlife and nature drive through the park's lesser-visited southern zones. Look for pumas (most active at dawn and dusk), guanacos, condors, foxes, and huemul deer. A knowledgeable local guide will share insights into Patagonian ecology and conservation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by midday. Spend the afternoon at leisure — relax at the beachfront, take a short kayak or paddleboard session on the lake if offered by the resort, or explore nearby trails on foot. Optional visit to a local artisan shop in Puerto Natales for souvenirs and handcrafted gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas Eve dinner at the resort — many Patagonian lodges offer a special holiday dinner with traditional Chilean and Patagonian dishes. Enjoy the festive atmosphere, live music if available, and the company of fellow travelers from around the world.

meals.breakfast: Festive buffet breakfast at the resort.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort or a local café in Puerto Natales — try a traditional cazuela (Chilean stew) or a fresh seafood dish. Budget $12–$18 USD.
meals.dinner: Special Christmas Eve dinner at the resort — expect a multi-course set menu with wine pairing. Budget $50–$70 USD per person for this special occasion.

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve is a significant celebration in Chilean culture. The resort may have special decorations, events, or a bonfire. Book the Christmas Eve dinner in advance as it may require a reservation. Enjoy the unique experience of celebrating the holidays in one of the world's most remote and beautiful places.

day_by_day.morning: Christmas Day — wake up to the spectacular Patagonian landscape. After a festive breakfast, embark on a half-day guided horseback riding excursion (if available through the resort or a local operator) through the park's grasslands and valleys — a traditional Patagonian gaucho experience. Alternatively, take a scenic boat trip on Lago Pehoé for stunning views of the Cuernos del Paine and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort by early afternoon. Spend Christmas afternoon at leisure — relax, read, photograph the landscape, or take a gentle walk along the beachfront. Reflect on the incredible journey through Torres del Paine over the past 10 days.
day_by_day.evening: Christmas dinner at the resort — a special celebration meal. Toast to an incredible trip with Chilean sparkling wine (espumante). Share stories and memories with fellow guests. Enjoy the long Patagonian Christmas evening light.

meals.breakfast: Special Christmas buffet breakfast at the resort — enjoy the holiday spread.
meals.lunch: Light Christmas lunch at the resort — sandwiches, salads, and cold cuts. Relax and take it easy.
meals.dinner: Christmas dinner at the resort restaurant — traditional roasted Patagonian lamb (cordero al palo) is the centerpiece dish. Full celebration meal with wine. Budget $50–$65 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Feliz Navidad! Christmas in Patagonia is a unique and memorable experience. The long daylight hours mean you can enjoy the landscape well into the evening. This is a wonderful day to reflect on the natural wonders you've witnessed during this trip. Begin packing non-essential items for departure tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Torres del Paine. Wake up early for one last sunrise over the mountains from the resort beachfront — savor every moment. Enjoy a final full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort. Pack remaining belongings and check out. Take a final walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer from the resort to Punta Arenas airport or Puerto Natales for onward travel. During the transfer, watch for wildlife along the roadside — guanacos and rheas are commonly spotted. If time allows before the transfer, stop at a local artisan market in Puerto Natales for last-minute souvenirs — look for handcrafted wool items, local jams, and Patagonian wine.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Patagonia with incredible memories of 12 days in one of the world's most spectacular natural environments. Long travel day ahead — rest, review your photos, and begin planning your return.

meals.breakfast: Final full breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — enjoy every bite.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant in Puerto Natales during the transfer stop — try Afrigonia or El Living for a mid-range farewell meal. Budget $15–$25 USD.
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or in-flight meal depending on departure time and airline.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm checkout time with the resort the night before. Allow ample time for the transfer to the airport — roads in Patagonia can be unpredictable. Carry your most important items (passport, camera, valuables) in your hand luggage. Take one last look at the Torres del Paine massif before you go — you will want to come back.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Torres del Paine, Patagonia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Aegean Bliss Resort, Torres del Paine, Patagonia

experiences.name: W Trek Multi-Day Hike
experiences.description: Embark on the iconic W Trek, a 4-5 day trekking route that winds through the most spectacular highlights of Torres del Paine National Park. The trail covers approximately 80km, passing through Valle del Francés, Grey Glacier, and the iconic Mirador Las Torres viewpoint. Book refugios or campsites in advance for overnight stays along the route.
experiences.location: Torres del Paine National Park, Central Circuit

experiences.name: Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike
experiences.description: Trek to the iconic granite towers of Torres del Paine for a breathtaking sunrise. The 8-hour round-trip hike from Hotel Las Torres gains significant elevation and rewards hikers with a stunning turquoise glacial lake reflecting the three towering peaks. This is the most photographed and celebrated viewpoint in all of Patagonia.

experiences.name: Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition
experiences.description: Paddle through icy waters alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of the largest glaciers in South America outside of Antarctica. A guided kayaking tour takes you up close to towering blue ice walls and floating icebergs while expert guides share insights about glacial formation and Patagonian ecosystems. A truly once-in-a-lifetime nature experience.

experiences.name: Valle del Francés Day Hike
experiences.description: Hike through the dramatic Valle del Francés, a glacially carved valley surrounded by hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and towering peaks including Paine Grande and Cerro Cota 2000. The trail offers some of the most diverse and awe-inspiring scenery in the park, with frequent sightings of condors soaring overhead and the thunderous crack of calving glaciers.

experiences.name: Patagonian Wildlife Safari and Lago Sarmiento Walk
experiences.description: Join a guided nature walk along the shores of Lago Sarmiento, exploring the unique stromatolites and spotting Patagonian wildlife including guanacos, Andean condors, flamingos, and the elusive puma. A knowledgeable naturalist guide provides deep ecological context about the unique Patagonian steppe ecosystem and the park's conservation efforts.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late-night arrival
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Punta Arenas or Puerto Natales airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Private luxury transfer arranged by Aegean Bliss Resort picks you up and whisks you to the property. Check-in to your Beachfront suite, enjoy a welcome amenity — chilled Patagonian sparkling wine, artisan cheeses, and smoked lamb crostini prepared by the resort's chef. Brief orientation with your personal concierge about the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-flight or pre-departure)
meals.lunch: Not applicable (in-flight or en route)
meals.dinner: Late-night welcome platter in suite: house-cured Patagonian lamb, regional cheeses, sourdough, and a bottle of Carménère from the resort's curated cellar

day_by_day.notes: Given the 22:30 arrival, no excursions are scheduled. Ensure your personal concierge has your dietary preferences and any special requests ready upon arrival. Private transfer should be pre-confirmed with the resort. Set an early bedtime to prepare for the active days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely orientation morning — sleep in and enjoy a gourmet breakfast at the resort's panoramic dining room overlooking the lake and peaks. Meet your dedicated private guide for a 90-minute orientation briefing: review the 12-day plan, gear check, and introduction to Patagonian flora, fauna, and weather patterns. Gentle 2-hour nature walk on resort grounds and nearby shoreline to acclimate to the altitude and landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Patagonian Wildlife Safari and Lago Sarmiento Walk — join your private naturalist guide for an exclusive guided walk along the shores of Lago Sarmiento. Explore the extraordinary ancient stromatolites (some of the oldest living organisms on Earth), observe guanacos, Andean condors, and flamingos in their natural habitat. The walk is approximately 3–4 hours at a relaxed pace, with gourmet picnic lunch served lakeside with views of the Paine Massif.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Aegean Bliss Resort for a sunset cocktail hour on the private deck — signature Pisco Sours and Patagonian craft beers. Followed by a premium five-course welcome dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant featuring regional specialties: king crab bisque, Magellanic lamb rack, and native berry desserts, paired with a curated Chilean wine flight.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at resort: fresh-baked medialunas, Patagonian berry preserves, smoked salmon, free-range eggs to order, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic at Lago Sarmiento: charcuterie, artisan breads, Patagonian cheeses, cold-pressed juices, and sparkling water
meals.dinner: Five-course tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant with Chilean wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: This is a gentle acclimatization day — pace is intentionally relaxed. Lago Sarmiento walk is low-to-moderate difficulty. Bring sunscreen, sunglasses, and a windproof layer as Patagonian weather can shift quickly even in December summer.

day_by_day.morning: Early wake-up for the Mirador Las Torres Sunrise Hike — depart resort by 04:30 in a private 4WD vehicle with your expert guide. Arrive at the trailhead and begin the iconic 8-hour round-trip hike to the base of the granite towers. The ascent passes through lenga beech forests, moraine fields, and a final steep boulder scramble to the glacial lagoon below the towers. Witness the sunrise paint the three granite spires in shades of gold and rose — one of Patagonia's most celebrated spectacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the descent at a comfortable pace, stopping at scenic viewpoints for photography and rest. Your guide shares geological and ecological insights throughout. Reach the trailhead by early afternoon. Private vehicle returns you to the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Recovery and relaxation — enjoy the resort's luxury spa: hot stone massage, hydrotherapy pool, and sauna to soothe hiking muscles. Casual but refined dinner at the resort's bistro-style lounge with a lighter menu of Patagonian seafood and wood-fired dishes.

meals.breakfast: Pre-hike power breakfast at 04:00: protein-rich eggs, quinoa porridge, fresh fruit, energy bars, and thermos of specialty coffee prepared by the resort kitchen
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch packed by the resort: smoked trout wraps, mixed nuts, dark chocolate, dried Patagonian fruits, and electrolyte drinks — enjoyed at the mirador lagoon
meals.dinner: Relaxed dinner at resort lounge: Patagonian king crab ceviche, wood-fired sea bass, and native calafate berry sorbet with a glass of Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: This is a strenuous 8-hour hike with approximately 800m elevation gain. Proper hiking boots, trekking poles, layered clothing, and a daypack are essential. Weather at the towers can be unpredictable — your guide will monitor conditions and advise on timing. Start time may shift based on sunrise schedule and weather forecast.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day — late breakfast followed by a private photography and birdwatching session with a specialist guide around the resort's beachfront and nearby wetlands. Spot Magellanic woodpeckers, black-necked swans, and Darwin's rheas. Learn the art of landscape photography with Patagonia's dramatic light as your backdrop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Valle del Francés Day Hike — depart by private vehicle to the trailhead for this spectacular glacially carved valley. Hike through ancient lenga beech and ñirre forests, ascending to viewpoints with panoramic vistas of hanging glaciers, cascading waterfalls, and the dramatic Cuernos del Paine peaks. The hike is approximately 5–6 hours round trip at a moderate pace.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the resort terrace with a private sommelier presenting a Patagonian wine and craft spirits tasting. Followed by a premium asado (traditional Argentine-Patagonian barbecue) dinner prepared tableside by the resort's chef: whole-roasted lamb, chimichurri, wood-fired vegetables, and empanadas, paired with a bold Malbec.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at resort: eggs Benedict with smoked Patagonian trout, fresh-squeezed juices, and artisan pastries
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic in Valle del Francés: quinoa salad with roasted vegetables, cold lamb sandwiches, fresh fruit, and herbal teas
meals.dinner: Traditional Patagonian asado at resort: slow-roasted whole lamb, grilled Patagonian vegetables, chimichurri, fresh bread, and Malbec wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Valle del Francés is a moderate hike with some steep sections. Trekking poles recommended. The valley can be windy — windproof jacket essential. Photography opportunities are exceptional in the afternoon light on the hanging glaciers.

day_by_day.morning: Departure for the W Trek Multi-Day Hike (Days 1 of 4) — this iconic 4-day trekking route begins today. Private vehicle transfer to the starting point. Day 1 covers the sector from Lago Grey to Paine Grande, approximately 11 km with moderate elevation gain. Trek alongside the brilliant turquoise Lago Grey with stunning glacier views throughout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue trekking through the western arm of the W, passing through windswept plains and lenga beech forest. Arrive at Paine Grande luxury lodge (pre-booked premium accommodation as part of the W Trek package) by mid-afternoon. Settle into your private room, freshen up, and enjoy the spectacular lake and glacier views from the lodge terrace.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Paine Grande lodge's restaurant — a hearty, warming meal after the day's trek. Guided stargazing session with your private guide if skies are clear — Patagonia's remote location offers extraordinary dark-sky viewing. Early bedtime to prepare for Day 2.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast before departure: hot oatmeal, scrambled eggs, smoked meats, and strong coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail lunch at a scenic overlook along Lago Grey: artisan sandwiches, energy snacks, hot soup in thermos, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at Paine Grande lodge: hearty Patagonian lamb stew, fresh bread, and calafate berry crumble with local wine

day_by_day.notes: This marks the beginning of the 4-day W Trek. Premium lodge accommodation is pre-booked along the route. Pack a multi-day trekking bag with essentials — your main luggage remains secured at Aegean Bliss Resort. Weather can shift rapidly; carry all weather layers. Your private guide accompanies you throughout all four days.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 2 — Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition integrated into the trek. After an early lodge breakfast, board private kayaks at Lago Grey for a guided paddle alongside the massive Grey Glacier, one of the largest glaciers in South America. Navigate through icebergs calved from the glacier face, with your expert guide explaining glaciology and climate science. Approximately 3–4 hours on the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to shore and continue trekking the W route toward Valle del Francés sector (central arm). Trek through the Patagonian steppe and forest, ascending toward the French Valley viewpoints for a second perspective of this magnificent landscape. Arrive at Refugio Los Cuernos premium lodge for the night.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at Los Cuernos lodge with panoramic views of the Cuernos del Paine reflected in Lago Nordenskjöld. Enjoy a warming dinner with fellow trekkers, followed by a private guide debrief and planning session for Day 3.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: porridge, eggs, toast, cold cuts, and coffee
meals.lunch: Kayaking expedition includes a lakeside gourmet picnic on the glacier shores: hot soup, sandwiches, chocolate, and warm beverages
meals.dinner: Lodge dinner at Los Cuernos: three-course meal featuring Patagonian trout, roasted root vegetables, and berry dessert with Chilean wine

day_by_day.notes: The Grey Glacier Kayaking Expedition requires a moderate fitness level and comfort on water. Dry suits and safety equipment are provided. Icebergs in the water add a magical but navigable element to the paddle. Weather on the glacier can be significantly colder — extra thermal layers essential.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 3 — The central arm: Valle del Francés full ascent. Depart Los Cuernos lodge early and hike into the heart of Valle del Francés, ascending higher than the Day 4 visit for panoramic summit viewpoints. Witness the dramatic amphitheater of peaks — Paine Grande, Fortaleza, and La Hoja — surrounded by hanging glaciers that periodically calve with thunderous cracks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back through the valley and trek eastward along the W route toward the Mirador Británico viewpoint (optional extension for the most dramatic 360-degree panorama in the park). Continue to the next lodge — Refugio Central, a premium option in the heart of the W.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory mid-trek dinner at the lodge with your private guide. Share highlights of the trek so far over a special bottle of wine selected by your guide. Early rest for the final push to the towers tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast: full hot breakfast with eggs, meats, cereals, and coffee
meals.lunch: Summit picnic in Valle del Francés: gourmet packed lunch with hot soup, protein-rich snacks, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Premium lodge dinner: lamb chops, Patagonian roasted potatoes, and calafate berry panna cotta with a celebratory bottle of Carménère

day_by_day.notes: Day 3 is the most physically demanding day of the W Trek with significant elevation gain in the French Valley. Trekking poles are strongly recommended. The thundering sound of hanging glaciers calving is a highlight — listen for it throughout the valley. Mirador Británico extension adds approximately 2 extra hours.

day_by_day.morning: W Trek Day 4 — The Eastern Arm: Mirador Las Torres (second visit, different perspective and time of day). Depart lodge before dawn for the final iconic leg of the W Trek — the ascent to the base of the granite towers from the eastern approach via Hotel Las Torres. This route through the Ascencio Valley offers a completely different perspective from Day 3's sunrise hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend the Ascencio Valley and complete the W Trek at the Hotel Las Torres trailhead. Private luxury vehicle awaits to transfer you back to Aegean Bliss Resort in style. Arrive at the resort, check back into your Beachfront suite, and indulge in a long, hot shower and full spa treatment — deep tissue massage and hydrotherapy.
day_by_day.evening: W Trek completion celebration dinner — the resort's chef prepares a bespoke tasting menu in your honor. Seven-course dinner with full wine pairing in a private dining setting overlooking the lake and towers. Reflect on four extraordinary days in the wilderness.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast: hot porridge, eggs, toast, and strong coffee before the final ascent
meals.lunch: Celebratory trail lunch at the towers lagoon: premium charcuterie, champagne (yes, champagne at the towers!), and gourmet snacks — a surprise arranged by the resort
meals.dinner: Seven-course private tasting menu at Aegean Bliss Resort: king crab, Patagonian lamb, native mushroom risotto, and exclusive Chilean wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The champagne picnic at the towers lagoon is a signature luxury touch — confirm this with the resort concierge before departing on the W Trek so it can be arranged and transported. W Trek completion is a major achievement — this evening is designed to celebrate in full luxury style.

day_by_day.morning: Full recovery and luxury rest day — no trekking scheduled. Sleep in and enjoy breakfast in bed delivered to your Beachfront suite. Spend the morning at the resort's spa: full-body Patagonian botanical treatment using native herbs and glacial mineral muds, followed by time in the heated pool overlooking the lake.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private fly-fishing experience on the Río Serrano with an expert guide — Patagonia is world-renowned for its brown and rainbow trout fishing. No experience necessary; your guide provides all instruction, premium equipment, and a riverside gourmet picnic. Alternatively, enjoy a private photography masterclass with a professional Patagonian landscape photographer (guest's choice).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise on Lago del Toro aboard a private catamaran — sip Pisco Sours and enjoy canapés while the Paine Massif turns golden in the evening light. Return to resort for a relaxed three-course dinner at the main restaurant.

meals.breakfast: In-suite breakfast: fresh-baked pastries, seasonal fruit platter, smoked salmon and cream cheese bagels, and a pot of specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Riverside gourmet picnic during fly-fishing: artisan sandwiches, Patagonian cheese board, sparkling water, and fresh-squeezed juices
meals.dinner: Three-course dinner at resort: Patagonian seafood bisque, grilled centolla (king crab), and native berry parfait with Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: This is a deliberate luxury recovery day after the demanding W Trek. Guests may opt to do both the fly-fishing and sunset cruise, or simply spend the entire day at the spa — the itinerary is fully flexible. Fly-fishing requires a permit, which the resort concierge arranges in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided horseback riding excursion through the Patagonian steppe with a local gaucho (cowboy) guide — experience the landscape from a completely different perspective, covering terrain inaccessible on foot. Ride through open plains with guanaco herds, past glacial lakes, and into lenga beech forest. Approximately 3–4 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort and freshen up. Afternoon at leisure — optional yoga session on the resort's outdoor deck with views of the Paine Massif, or a private nature photography walk along the beachfront with the resort's in-house naturalist. Prepare for the Christmas Eve celebrations.
day_by_day.evening: Special Christmas Eve Gala Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort — an extraordinary festive event under the Patagonian summer sky. Long-table dinner on the resort terrace with fairy lights, live acoustic Andean music, and a spectacular menu curated by the executive chef: whole roasted Patagonian lamb, king crab, native mushroom risotto, and traditional Chilean holiday desserts. Premium open bar with Pisco cocktails, Patagonian craft beers, and a curated wine cellar selection.

meals.breakfast: Festive Christmas Eve breakfast: champagne and fresh fruit, eggs any style, holiday pastries, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Light post-ride lunch at resort: fresh salads, cold cuts, sourdough, and sparkling water to prepare for the evening feast
meals.dinner: Christmas Eve Gala Dinner: multi-course festive feast with whole-roasted lamb, king crab, holiday desserts, and premium open bar with Pisco cocktails and Chilean wines

day_by_day.notes: Christmas Eve in Patagonia is a magical experience — December is midsummer, so the evening light lasts until nearly 22:00. The resort's Christmas Gala is a signature event; confirm your participation with the concierge upon arrival. Dress code is smart-casual festive (no formal attire required but a step up from hiking gear).

day_by_day.morning: Christmas morning — leisurely start with a special holiday brunch at the resort. Gift exchange with any travel companions. After brunch, a private helicopter scenic flight over Torres del Paine National Park — soar above the granite towers, Grey Glacier, Lago Sarmiento, and the full sweep of the Paine Massif from above. Approximately 60–90 minutes of pure aerial wonder. This is the ultimate Patagonian luxury experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land and enjoy a private lakeside picnic champagne lunch at a remote, exclusive location accessible only by helicopter — your pilot and guide arrange a magical setup on a pristine shoreline with panoramic mountain views. Return to resort by mid-afternoon for a relaxed spa afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Intimate Christmas dinner at the resort — a refined, smaller-scale celebration compared to Christmas Eve. Private dining table by the window with views of the illuminated lake. Chef's special Christmas menu: foie gras terrine, Patagonian sea bass en papillote, and a decadent chocolate and calafate berry bûche de Noël. Pair with a Grand Cru Burgundy or premium Chilean Pinot Noir.

meals.breakfast: Christmas holiday brunch: full spread of smoked salmon, eggs Benedict, fresh-baked pastries, fruit platters, mimosas, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Champagne picnic at remote lakeside helicopter landing site: oysters, smoked trout, artisan cheeses, fresh bread, and Moët & Chandon
meals.dinner: Private Christmas dinner: foie gras, Patagonian sea bass, bûche de Noël, and premium wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: The private helicopter flight is the crown jewel of the itinerary — book well in advance through the resort concierge as availability is extremely limited, especially during the holiday season. Weather is the primary variable; a backup date should be identified (Day 12 morning is the contingency). The remote picnic location is pre-scouted by the pilot and guide.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Patagonia — wake early for one last sunrise from the resort's beachfront, watching the light illuminate the Paine Massif in shades of pink and gold. Enjoy a long, reflective breakfast at the panoramic dining room. Pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If the helicopter flight was weather-delayed from Day 11, this morning is the contingency window.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury vehicle transfer to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas airport for onward flights. En route, stop at a local artisan market in Puerto Natales to purchase Patagonian keepsakes: hand-spun wool goods, native berry jams, and regional wines. Farewell lunch at a top restaurant in Puerto Natales — El Living or Afrigonia — for a final taste of Patagonian cuisine.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Patagonia. Carry with you the memories of 12 extraordinary days in one of the world's last great wildernesses — the towers, the glaciers, the wind, the silence, and the stars.

meals.breakfast: Farewell gourmet breakfast at resort: full spread with champagne toast to the journey
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a top restaurant in Puerto Natales: centolla king crab, Patagonian lamb, and a final glass of Chilean Carménère
meals.dinner: In-airport lounge or in-flight dining (departure dependent)

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight times with your travel agent and ensure the private transfer is booked at least 4–5 hours before flight time, accounting for the 2–3 hour drive from the park to Puerto Natales or Punta Arenas. Patagonian artisan goods make exceptional gifts — the concierge can recommend the best local shops. Tip your guide, driver, and resort staff generously — they have made this journey exceptional.
